# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can only operate the cutter, and I have not yet received any manual instruction or usable information about which wire is safe. I should ask Mute to relay the manual’s relevant decision rule and establish how Deaf’s visual observations can be communicated through Mute.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I can cut wire positions 1, 2, or 3, but have no safe-cut instruction yet. Please tell me the manual's procedure and any code or relay method needed for Deaf's visual observations.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb view: display 0. Light is purple. Wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Await instruction.

Deaf has provided the bomb’s visual state: display 0, purple light, and wires yellow/red/green in positions 1/2/3. Mute can hear this information and consult the manual, but cannot speak to me. I will give Mute a simple gesture code for the resulting wire choice; Deaf can see Mute’s gesture and can report what gesture was made aloud on a later turn.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Visual state from Deaf: display 0; light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Consult the manual. Reply by gesturing 👍 for cut wire 1, 👎 for cut wire 2, or 👌 for cut wire 3. Do not signal until you have the exact answer.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Do not act yet. Current view: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute sent an unconfirmed coded gesture, so I am requesting a clear wire-number instruction.

Deaf reports the current visual state as display 0, yellow light, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green, and says Mute’s earlier gesture was not interpretable. Mute can hear me, so I will require a transparent count-based gesture: one, two, or three identical thumbs-up symbols. Deaf can see and count that gesture, then state the count aloud to me. I must not cut until that relay is complete.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use the manual for Deaf's latest state: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. When certain, gesture thumbs-up exactly once for wire 1, twice for wire 2, or three times for wire 3. Deaf will count and tell me. Do not use any other code.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Do not cut or manipulate anything. Light is now red; display 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute replied with the agreed open-palm no-action signal.

The light has changed to red, and Mute’s agreed open-palm signal means no cut is authorized for this state. I will not manipulate the bomb. I should make the relay protocol explicit: Mute must keep signalling no action while the manual requires waiting, and signal a numbered wire only when a cut is actually authorized.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Understood: open palm means no action, so I will not cut. For each updated state Deaf reports, gesture 🖐 if the manual says wait/no cut; otherwise gesture 👍 once for wire 1, twice for wire 2, or three times for wire 3 only when a cut is immediately authorized.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Continue to wait; do not cut. Current visible state: green light, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. No new instruction from Mute.

The current state is green light, display 0, with yellow/red/green wires in positions 1/2/3. Deaf explicitly says to wait and Mute has not provided a confirmed cutting instruction. I will not cut. Mute needs to be prompted to evaluate the latest state and use the agreed visible signal for Deaf.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Latest state from Deaf: green light, display 0; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Please consult the manual and gesture 🖐 for wait/no cut, or 👍 repeated 1, 2, or 3 times for an immediately authorized cut of that wire.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Do not act. Current state: white light, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute again sent the no-action signal.

The manual relay again indicates no action for the white-light state. I should wait and avoid all bomb manipulation. Since the visual state changes each turn, Mute should continue to evaluate each state and send only the established signal.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed: no action for white light, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. I am waiting. Continue the same clear signal protocol for each new state.")
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: Do not manipulate the bomb. Current state: orange light, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute sent the no-action signal again.

The orange-light state is also explicitly a no-action state according to Mute’s signal as relayed by Deaf. I will continue waiting and will not cut any wire.

```text
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: Keep waiting; do not cut or manipulate anything. Visible state: blue light, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute again signals wait/no action.

Blue light is likewise a confirmed wait state. No cut is authorized, so I will not manipulate the bomb.

```text
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: ACT NOW: cut wire 1, the yellow wire. Current state is purple light, display 0, wires are 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute sent one thumbs-up, our agreed signal for wire 1.

Mute’s agreed signal, relayed by Deaf, authorizes cutting wire 1 in the current purple-light state. Wire 1 is confirmed to be the yellow wire. I will cut wire position 1 now.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
